The Petitioner before this Court has filed this present petition as a Public Interest Litigation ('PIL') stating that in the monsoon season this year, on account of flooding in Yamuna River, the water level crossed danger level of 205.33 and large numbers of persons in NCT of Delhi stood displaced.
The Petitioner submits that around 25,000 people, apart from livestock, were directly or indirectly affected by the floods.

In the prayer clause, the following reliefs are sought:

2. Today, there is no appearance on behalf of the Petitioner.
We note that this Court issued notice in the matter on 24th July, 2023 and the Government of NCT of Delhi ("GNCTD") has filed a detailed status report.
Copy thereof has been handed across the board and we have perused the same.
Per the report, a "Flood Control Order" is issued every year in Delhi in the last week of June, which contains the details of agencies engaged in flood control management.
Further, an "Apex Committee" chaired by the Chief Minister, is in existence in Delhi which recommends, supervises and co-ordinates flood control measures.
To assist the Apex Committee, a "Central Control Room" is set up every year from 15th June to 15th October at L.M. Bund, Shastri Nagar, which functions round the clock.
It is stated that, for this year, the Flood Control Order-2023 was released on 06th July, 2023 and the Control Room was duly set up on 15th June, 2023.
Said Control Room would be operational till 15th October, 2023 or till the withdrawal of the monsoon season.
3. The report also contains details of the measures in place to tackle floods and the steps taken in light of the flooding situation in NCT of Delhi this year.

The Central Water Commission (CWC)
shares advisory and flood forecasts with agencies, and when an advisory is received, the Standard Operating Procedures under the Flood Control Order-2023 are put into effect.

The concerned agencies are also cognizant of the water level in Delhi, and when the level crosses the danger mark,
measures are taken towards evacuation.
This year, prior to the rise in water level, a regular munadi (public announcement) was carried out by the Revenue Administration and Police to sensitize people of the possibility of flooding

In fact, in the beginning of July,
boats were deployed by Irrigation and Flood Control Department as also the National Disaster Relief Force, and people along with their livestock were evacuated to safety.
Civil Defence Volunteers were also deployed in large numbers to augment evacuation efforts.

Notably, this year,
on 13th July, 2023, the water level reached 208.66 meters at the Old Railway Bridge, which is the highest ever.
4. Around 27,381 persons were evacuated from flood-affected low-lying areas and a total of 47 relief camps were established across 6 districts of NCT of Delhi.
This included temporary camps as well as camps in pucca buildings i.e., schools, community centres etc.
Government officers of various departments were deployed to ensure availability of facilities in every camp.
Basic necessities such as food, water, medicines, sanitation, bedding etc. were made available by various departments and organisations in these camps round the clock.
Specifically, drinking and bathing water was made available through the Delhi Jal Board.
Shelter was provided by way of water-proof tents at some camps.
Cleanliness and hygiene were maintained by MCD staff, which also carried out fumigation in each camp.
Mobile toilets, electricity connections, fans, bedding, sanitary pads, etc. were also made available along with hot cooked food for inhabitants at each camp.
